_note: SAFETY HARD-BLOCK THRESHOLDS (v3, 26 Nov 2026 — adds a spearfishing current limit). Set from published BOM, WA Department of Transport and Recfishwest guidance, choosing the cautious end. NOT reviewed on site by a safety professional — users must always judge conditions themselves. Estuary spots ignore wave limits (no ocean waves).

thresholds.rationale: Very strong gusts — risk of being blown off jetties, groynes and walls
basis: BOM strong wind warning: 25–33 knots (45–60 km/h); gusts can be 40% stronger
BOM strong wind warning: 25–33 knots (45–60 km/h); gusts can be 40% stronger

thresholds.rationale: Large waves reaching the shore — single waves can be twice this
basis: BOM dangerous-surf thresholds (2007 study): onshore waves 3–4 m at 10 s+, or over 4 m
BOM / WA DoT: the biggest waves can be up to twice the forecast (significant) wave height

thresholds.rationale: Long-period swell (14 s+) — powerful surges run far up beaches and over groynes
basis: BOM dangerous-surf thresholds (2007 study): onshore waves 3–4 m at 10 s+, or over 4 m
BOM / WA DoT: the biggest waves can be up to twice the forecast (significant) wave height

thresholds.rationale: Rocks: waves over 1.5 m from any direction — waves wrap around headlands
basis: Experienced rock fishers (NSW): onshore swell over 1.4 m treated as dangerous on an exposed platform
BOM / WA DoT: the biggest waves can be up to twice the forecast (significant) wave height

thresholds.rationale: Rocks: long-period swell (13 s+) over 1 m — sets surge without warning
basis: Recfishwest safety ambassador Chris Dixon: no rock fishing facing the swell when period is over 16 s or rising
BOM / WA DoT: the biggest waves can be up to twice the forecast (significant) wave height

thresholds.rationale: Rocks: swell period 16 s or longer — rogue-wave conditions
basis: Recfishwest safety ambassador Chris Dixon: no rock fishing facing the swell when period is over 16 s or rising

thresholds.rationale: Rocks: strong gusts on wet rock
basis: BOM strong wind warning: 25–33 knots (45–60 km/h); gusts can be 40% stronger

thresholds.rationale: Rocks: no wave forecast, so rock safety can't be checked
basis: App rule: unknown is treated as unsafe on rocks

thresholds.rationale: Swell too big for safe shore entry and exit
basis: BOM / WA DoT: the biggest waves can be up to twice the forecast (significant) wave height

thresholds.rationale: Long-period swell (14 s+) — surge at entry/exit points and in caves
basis: Recfishwest safety ambassador Chris Dixon: no rock fishing facing the swell when period is over 16 s or rising
BOM / WA DoT: the biggest waves can be up to twice the forecast (significant) wave height

thresholds.rationale: Wind over 25 km/h — chop, drift and hard to see your float
basis: BOM boating safety: winds over 15 knots (28 km/h) not suitable for small vessels
WA DoT 'Weather or not': over 20 knots (37 km/h) unsafe for small craft; 3 m craft safe only to 8 knots
WA DoT 'Weather or not': over 20 knots (37 km/h) unsafe for small craft; 3 m craft safe only to 8 knots

thresholds.rationale: No wave forecast, so diving safety can't be checked
basis: App rule: unknown is treated as unsafe for diving

thresholds.rationale: Very strong ocean current forecast — too strong for a breath-hold diver to swim against
basis: A fit diver with fins can hold about 2–3 km/h (1–1.5 knots) for a short time; dive guidance treats currents over 1 knot as strong
Model: Météo-France currents via Open-Meteo, ~8 km grid — shows offshore drift, not rips or channels near the shore
